page: Microsoft Azure D4ads_v6 is a general purpose virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The server is configured with 4 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. Cache architecture includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Memory allocation totals 16.0 GB RAM, presenting a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance lacks dedicated hardware acceleration with zero GPUs, but it bundles 236 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside premium storage capabilities. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512 (F, VNNI, and BF16), alongside hardware cryptography via AES and SHA-NI.

Benchmark analysis reflects strong single-thread CPU execution juxtaposed with mid-tier multi-threaded and memory-bound throughput. Single-core stress-ng tests reached 3079.47 and Geekbench single-core scored 1987.0, both placing in the top quartile. Text processing in Geekbench was similarly robust at 2488.0. Conversely, multi-threaded stress-ng (6156.76) and PassMark CPU score (7553.4) aligned with median expectations for a 4-vCPU system. Memory bandwidth measured 37.93 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 28.17 GB/sec for writes, leading to bottom-quartile metrics in intensive compilation (Geekbench Clang at 5344.0), Redis SET throughput (5.92 million operations/sec), and PassMark database operations (2013.9).

Given its hardware profile, the D4ads_v6 delivers solid density and computational efficiency for small to mid-scale enterprise workloads that do not demand extensive RAM bandwidth or large-scale parallelism. CPU-bound tasks requiring high per-core burst frequencies benefit from the AMD EPYC platform, while the integrated 236 GB NVMe SSD provides low-latency local scratch space for temporary caching and staging without requiring external detached disks.

The instance is well suited for web serving workloads, small-scale microservices, lightweight application backends, and text-processing pipelines. Workloads involving heavy database I/O, large-scale concurrent compiling, or medium-to-large language model inference face architectural bottlenecks due to memory bandwidth and physical core limits.
description: Microsoft Azure D4ads_v6 is a general purpose instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 x86_64 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz, delivering 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores. It features 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, and includes 236 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage with no bundled GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core CPU throughput, highlighted by high Geekbench single-core and text processing metrics, while multi-core compute, encryption, and static web serving yield average scores. However, uncached memory bandwidth constraints limit database operations, Clang compilation, and multi-threaded decompression. The instance offers a balanced resource profile for general application hosting, web serving, text pipelines, and development workloads requiring fast local scratch storage.
